body.text: Aṣṭādaśasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā, Parivartas 55 - 70
body.translated_text: <s>Aṣṭādaśasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>, <s>Parivartas</s> 55 - 70

body.text:
Parivarta 55.
[f. 215b] atha bhagavān ayuṣmantaṃ subhūtim etad avocat: sacet punaḥ subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ svapnāntaragato 'pi śrāvakabhūmaye vā pratyekabuddhabhūmaye vā traidhātukāya vā na spṛhayate, na anuśamsācittam utpādayati, svapnopamān eva sarvadharman vyavalokayati, pratiśrutkopamān yāvan nirmitopamān eva sarvadharmān vyavalokayati, na ca sākṣātkaroti. idaṃ subhūte avaivartikasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya-avaivartikalakṣaṇaṃ veditavyam. punar aparaṃ subhūte saced bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ svapnāntaragato 'py anekaśataparivāram anekasahasraparivāraṃ anekaśatasahasraparivāram anekakoṭīparivāram anekakoṭīsahasraparivāram anekakoṭīśatasahasraparivāram anekakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraparivāraṃ bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikābhir devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragaiḥ parivṛtaṃ puraskṛtaṃ tathāgatam arhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ dharman deśayantaṃ paśyati, sa tan dharmaṃ śrutvā tasya dharmasya artham ājñāsyāmi iti iti, dharmānudharmapratipanno viharati, sāmīcīpratipanno 'nudharmacārī. idam api subhūte avaivartikasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyaiva avaivarkalakṣaṇaṃ veditavyam. punar aparaṃ subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ svapnāntaragato 'pi tathāgatam arhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ paśyati, vaihāyasam abhyudgamya bhikṣusaṃghāya dharmaṃ deśayantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ (

children.translated_text: AdSPG I 4

children.text: ) samanvāgataṃ vyāmaprabhām ṛddhiprātihāryāṇi sandarśayantaṃ nirmitāni ca nirmimāṇaṃ yāni nirmitāny anyeṣu lokadhātuṣu buddhakaryāṇi kurvanti. idam api subhūte avaivartikasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya avaivartikalakṣaṇaṃ veditavyam. punar aparaṃ subhūte sacet svapnāntaragato bodhisattvo mahāsattvo nottrasyati na santrasyati na santrāsam āpadyate, grāmaghāte vā vartamāne nagaraghāte vā vartamāne agnidāhe vā vartamāne, vyādamṛgān vā dṛṣṭvā tadanyāni vā cāṇḍālamṛgajātāni dṛṣṭvā, śirṣacchedaṃ vā pratyupasthitaṃ dṛṣṭvā, yān vā tadanyāṃ bhayabhairavāṃ saṃtrāsāṃ dṛṣṭvā, duḥkhadaurmanasya-upāyāsāṃ dṛṣṭvā, jighatsitaṃ vā pipāsitaṃ vā dṛṣṭvā, mātṛmaraṇaṃ vā pitṛmaraṇaṃ vā bhrātṛmaraṇaṃ vā bhaginīmaraṇaṃ vā dṛṣṭvā, mitrajñātisālohitamaraṇaṃ vā dṛṣṭvā na śokabhayai bhairavaḥ saṃtrāsa utpādyate. tataś ca svapnāt samanantaraprativibuddhasya sata evaṃ bhavati: svapnopamaṃ vatedaṃ sarvatraidhātukaṃ, mayāpy anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbudhya svapnopamāḥ sarvatraidhātukadharmā deśayitavyāḥ. idam api subhūte avaivartikasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya avaivartikalakṣaṇaṃ veditavyam. punar aparaṃ subhūte kathaṃ vijñāyate, yad avaivartikasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhasya tatra buddhakṣetre sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathā sarvaṃ trayo 'pāyā na bhaviṣyanti? sacet svapnāntaragato 'pi bodhisattvo [f. 216a?] mahāsattvo nairayikān vā sattvān dṛṣṭvā tiryagyonikān vā sattvān dṛṣṭvā yamalaukikān vā sattvān dṛṣṭvā evaṃ smṛtiṃ pratilabhate, smṛtipratilabdhasyaivaṃ bhavati tathā kariṣyāmi tathā pratipatsye yathā me 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhasya tatra buddhakṣetre (
children.translated_text: ) with a fathom-wide radiance, displaying miraculous feats of supernatural power, and creating emanations that perform the work of a Buddha in other world-systems — this too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be known as the mark of non-regression of a non-regressing <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>. Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, if a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> within a dream is not terrified, is not alarmed, does not become frightened — when a village is being destroyed, when a city is being destroyed, when a fire is burning, upon seeing wild beasts or other fierce animals of low birth, upon seeing decapitation imminent, upon seeing whatever other fears, terrors, and frights, upon seeing suffering, grief, and distress, upon seeing hunger or thirst, upon seeing the death of a mother, the death of a father, the death of a brother, or the death of a sister, or upon seeing the death of friends, relatives, and kinsmen — no grief, fear, terror, or fright arises. And immediately upon awakening from that dream, this thought occurs to him: 'All this triple world is indeed dream-like. Having attained unsurpassed perfect and full awakening, I too should teach that all dharmas of the triple world are dream-like.' This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be known as the mark of non-regression of a non-regressing <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>. Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, how is it to be known that a non-regressing <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, having attained unsurpassed perfect and full awakening, will have in that buddha-field absolutely and completely no three lower destinies whatsoever? If a <s>Bodhisattva</s> [f. 216a?] <s>Mahāsattva</s>, even while within a dream, upon seeing beings in the hells, or beings in animal births, or beings in the world of <s>Yama</s>, attains this mindfulness, and having attained mindfulness thinks thus: 'I shall so act, I shall so practice, that in my buddha-field, having attained unsurpassed perfect and full awakening (
AdSPG I 5

children.text: ) sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathā sarvaṃ trayo 'pāyā na bhaviṣyanti, tat kasya hetos? tathā hi yaś ca svapno yaś ca svapnāntaḥ sarvam etad advayam advaidhīkāram. idam api subhūte avaivartikasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya avaivartikalakṣaṇaṃ veditavyam. punar aparaṃ subhūte saced bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ svapnāntaragato vā vibuddho vā nagaradāhe vā vartamāne evaṃ samanvāharati: ye mayā svapnānataragatena vā vibuddhena vā ākārā yāni liṅgāni yāni nimittāni dṛṣṭāni, yair ākārair yair liṅgair yair nimittaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'vaivartiko veditavyaḥ, sacet me te ākārās tāni liṅgāni tāni nimittāni saṃvidyante, anena satyena satyavacanena ayaṃ nagaradāha upaśāmyatu śītībhavatv astaṃ gacchatu, sacet pratiśāmyati śītībhavaty astaṃ gacchati, veditavyaṃ subhūte, vyākṛto 'yaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'nuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodher avaivartikatāyām. sacet punaḥ subhūte so 'gniskandhas tat satyavacanam atikramya gṛhād gṛhaṃ dahaty, rathyāyā rathyāyāṃ dahaty, anyāni gṛhāni dahaty anyāni gṛhāni na dahaty, anyāḥ rathyā dahaty anyāḥ rathyā na dahati, veditavyaṃ subhūte tena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena dharmapratyākhyānasaṃvartanīyam ebhiḥ sattvaiḥ karmopacitaṃ yenaiṣāṃ sattvānām ekatyāni gṛhāni dahyanta ekatyāni gṛhāni na dahyante. teṣām etad dṛṣṭadhārmikaṃ karma vipacyate. tata evaitad dharmapratyākhyānāt sāvaśeṣaṃ karma vipacyate. ayaṃ subhūte hetur ayaṃ pratyaya avaivartikasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya, yair hetubhir yaiḥ pratyayair avaivartiko bodhisattvo mahāsattvo veditavyaḥ. punar aparaṃ subhūte yair ākārair yair liṅgair yair nimittair avaivartiko bodhisattvo mahāsattvo veditavyaḥ, tāny (
children.translated_text: ) there will be absolutely and completely no three lower destinies whatsoever.' For what reason? Because the dream and what is within the dream — all that is non-dual and undivided. This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be known as the mark of non-regression of a non-regressing <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>. Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, if a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, whether within a dream or awake, when a city is burning, reflects thus: 'Whatever signs, marks, and indications I have seen while within a dream or awake — the signs, marks, and indications by which a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> is to be known as non-regressing — if those signs, those marks, those indications are present in me, then by this truth, by this truthful declaration, may this city fire be pacified, may it become cool, may it be extinguished.' If it is pacified, becomes cool, and is extinguished, then it should be known, <s>Subhūti</s>, that this <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> has been predicted for the non-regression from unsurpassed perfect and full awakening. But if, <s>Subhūti</s>, that mass of fire, overcoming that truthful declaration, burns from house to house, burns from street to street, burns some houses and does not burn others, burns some streets and does not burn others — it should be known, <s>Subhūti</s>, that karma has been accumulated by those beings that results in the rejection of the Dharma, on account of which some houses of those beings burn and some do not. Their karma ripens in this very life. From that very rejection of the Dharma, residual karma ripens. This, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the cause, this is the condition of a non-regressing <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, the causes and conditions by which a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> is to be known as non-regressing. Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the signs, marks, and indications by which a non-regressing <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> is to be known — those (
AdSPG I 6

children.text:
) ākārās tāni liṅgāni tani nimittāni deśayiṣyāmi. sacet subhūte kācid eva strī vā puruṣo vā amanuṣyeṇa adhiṣṭhito bhavet, tatra bodhisattvena mahāsattvenaivaṃ samanvāhartavyaṃ: saced ahaṃ vyākṛtas taiḥ paurvakais tathāgatair arhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhair anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau parisamyaksaṃbuddhair anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariśuddho me 'dhyāśayo yathā
aham anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃboddhukāmo yathā aham anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃboddhukāmo yathā aham anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbhotsye pariśuddhaś ca me manasikāro 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, apagataṃ me śrāvakacittam apagataṃ me pratyekabuddhacittam, apagataśrāvākapratyekabuddhacittena anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhir abhisaṃboddhavyā, na ahaṃ na anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbhotsye, abhisaṃbhotsya eva aham anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim. ye te 'pi te asaṃkhyeya-aprameyeṣu lokadhātuṣu buddhā bhagavantas tiṣṭhanti dhṛyante yāpayanti dharmañ ca deśayanti, na teṣāṃ tathāgatānām arhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ kiṃcid ajñātam adṛṣṭam aviditam asākṣātkṛtam anabhisaṃbuddham. yathā me te buddhā bhagavanto jānanty āśayam iti hi [f. 216b] aham anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbhotsye. anena satyena satyavacanena iyaṃ strī vā puruṣo vā yena amanuṣyeṇa gṛhīto vā viheṭhito vā so 'manuṣyo 'pakrāmatu. sacet subhūte so 'manuṣyas tato na apakrāmati, tasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyaivaṃ bhāṣamāṇasya, veditavyaṃ subhūte na ayaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvo vyākṛtas taiḥ paurvakais tathāgatair arhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhair anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau. sacet (
children.translated_text: ) signs, marks, and indications I shall teach. If, <s>Subhūti</s>, some woman or man is possessed by a non-human being, therein the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> should reflect thus: 'If I have been predicted by those former <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly and fully awakened ones for unsurpassed perfect and full awakening, if my aspiration is pure — just as I desire to attain unsurpassed perfect and full awakening, just as I desire to attain unsurpassed perfect and full awakening, just as I shall attain unsurpassed perfect and full awakening, and my mental application toward unsurpassed perfect and full awakening is pure, the thought of a <s>Śrāvaka</s> has departed from me, the thought of a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> has departed from me, with a mind free from the thoughts of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> I shall attain unsurpassed perfect and full awakening, I will not fail to attain unsurpassed perfect and full awakening, I will certainly attain unsurpassed perfect and full awakening. Those Buddhas and Blessed Ones who abide, endure, and live in innumerable, immeasurable world-systems, teaching the Dharma — nothing is unknown, unseen, uncomprehended, unrealized, or unawakened to by those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly and fully awakened ones. As those Buddhas and Blessed Ones know my aspiration, [f. 216b] so indeed I shall attain unsurpassed perfect and full awakening. By this truth, by this truthful declaration, may this woman or man be released by the non-human being by whom she or he is seized or afflicted — may that non-human being depart.' If, <s>Subhūti</s>, that non-human being does not depart when the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> speaks thus, it should be known, <s>Subhūti</s>, that this <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> has not been predicted by those former <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly and fully awakened ones for unsurpassed perfect and full awakening. If (
AdSPG I 7

children.text: ) punaḥ subhūte bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyaivaṃ bhāṣamāṇasya so 'manuṣyabhūto 'pakrāmati, veditavyaṃ subhūte vyākṛto vatāyaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvas taiḥ paurvakais tathāgatair arhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhair anuttarasyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau. ebhiḥ subhūte ākārair ebhi liṅgair ebhi nimittaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ avaivartiko veditavyaḥ. punar aparaṃ subhūte bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya ṣaṭsu pāramitāsv acaritasya, upāyakauśalavirahitasya, acaritāvinaś caturṣu smṛtyupasthāneṣu yāvac chūnyatānimittāpraṇihiteṣu vimokṣamukheṣu, bodhisattvanyāmam anavakrāntasya satyādhiṣṭhānena māraḥ pāpīyān upasaṃkramiṣyati. sacet subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ satyādhiṣṭhānaṃ kariṣyati: yena satyena satyavacanena ahaṃ vyākṛto 'nuttarasyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau taiḥ paurvakais tathāgatair arhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaiḥ, anena satyena satyavacanena ayam amanuṣyabhūto 'pakrāmatu. tatra māraḥ pāpīyān autsukyam āpatsyate, kim ity ayam amanuṣyabhūto 'pakrāmet. tata kasya hetos? tathā hi māraḥ pāpīyān balavattaraṃ ca tejovattaraṃ ca tatra autsukyam āpatsyate, katham ayam amanuṣya ito 'pakrāmed iti. evaṃ sa māra adhiṣṭhānena tato 'pakramiṣyati. evaṃ ca tasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bhaviṣyati: mamaiṣo 'nubhāvena amanuṣyo 'pakrānto. na punar evaṃ jñāsyati: mārānubhāvenaiṣo 'manuṣyo 'pakrānta iti. sa tena anyān bodhisattvān mahāsattvān avamaṃsyate ullapiṣyati uccagghiṣyati kutsayiṣyati paṃsayiṣyaty: ahaṃ vyākṛto 'nuttarasyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau taiḥ paurvakais tathāgatair arhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhair, ete punar anye na vyākṛtā anuttarasyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, (
children.translated_text: ) however, <s>Subhūti</s>, when the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> speaks thus, that non-human being departs, it should be known, <s>Subhūti</s>, that this <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> has indeed been predicted by those former <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly and fully awakened ones for unsurpassed perfect and full awakening. With these signs, <s>Subhūti</s>, with these marks, with these indications, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> is to be known as non-regressing. Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, when a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> who has not practiced the six <s>pāramitās</s>, who is devoid of skill in means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>), who has not practiced the four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>) up to the gates of liberation — emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, and who has not entered the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s certainty of attainment (<s>bodhisattvanyāma</s>), makes a truth-declaration (<s>satyādhiṣṭhāna</s>), <s>Māra</s> the Evil One will approach. If, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> makes this truth-declaration: 'By this truth, by this truthful declaration — that I have been predicted for unsurpassed perfect and full awakening by those former <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly and fully awakened ones — may this non-human being depart,' thereupon <s>Māra</s> the Evil One will become anxious, wondering 'What if this non-human being departs?' For what reason? Because <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, being mightier and more powerful, will become anxious there, thinking 'How might this non-human depart from here?' Thus by the power of <s>Māra</s>'s intervention, that being will depart. And the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> will think: 'By my own power this non-human being has departed.' But he will not understand: 'By the power of <s>Māra</s> this non-human being has departed.' On that account he will look down upon, disparage, mock, belittle, and defame other <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, saying: 'I have been predicted for unsurpassed perfect and full awakening by those former <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly and fully awakened ones, but these others have not been predicted for unsurpassed perfect and full awakening' (
AdSPG I 8

children.text: ) sa tāvanmātrakeṇa mānaṃ vardhayiṣyati mānam utpādayiṣyati, dūrīkariṣyati sarvākārajñatāṃ dūrīkariṣyaty anuttaraṃ buddhajñānam. sa tathārūpo sattvas tāvatā anupāyakuśalo 'dhimānam utpādayiṣyati, tasya dve bhūmī pratikāṅkṣitavye. katame dve bhūmī? yaduta śrāvakabhūmir vā pratyekabuddhabhūmir vā. evaṃ satyādhiṣṭhānena tasya bodhisattvasy a mahāsattvasya mārakarmotpatsyate. tatra kalyāṇamitrāṇi na seviṣyati na pratiseviṣyati na bhakṣiṣyati na paryupāsiṣyate. tad eva mārabandhanaṃ gāḍhīkariṣyati. tat kasya hetos? tathāpi ca ṣaṭpāramitāsv acaritvāt upāyakauśalena ca aparigṛhītatvāt. evam api subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena mārakarma veditavyam. kathaṃ ca subhūte bodhisattvaṃ ṣaṭpāramitāsv acaritāvinaṃ yāvad anavakrāntanyāmaṃ nāmādhiṣṭhānena māraḥ pāpīyān upasaṃkramiṣyati? iha subhūte māraḥ pāpīyān anyatarānyatareṇa veṣeṇopasaṃkramya bodhisattvam evaṃ vakṣyati: vyākṛtas tvaṃ kulaputra tathāgatena arhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena anuttarasyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau [f. 217a?] idan te nāmadheyam idan te mātur nāmadheyam idan te pitur nāmadheyam idan te bhrātur nāmadheyam idan te bhaginyā nāmadheyam imāni te mitrāmātyajñātisālohitānāṃ nāmadheyāni. yāvad ā saptamasya mātāpitṛyugasya nāmadheyam upadekṣyaty, amuṣmāt tvaṃ janapadād amuṣyā diśo 'muṣmiṃ tvaṃ janapade jāto 'muṣmiṃ nagare vā grāme vā. sa sacet prakṛtyā mṛduko bhaviṣyati, sa enam evaṃ vakṣyati: pūrvāntato 'pi tvam evaṃ mṛduko 'bhūḥ. sacet tīkṣṇo bhaviṣyati, sa enam evaṃ vakṣyati: pūrvāntato 'pi tvam evaṃ tīkṣṇo 'bhūḥ. saced āraṇyako bhaviṣyati sacet piṇḍapātiko bhaviṣyati (
children.translated_text: ) He will increase his conceit by that much, he will generate conceit, he will distance himself from the knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>), he will distance himself from the unsurpassed Buddha-knowledge. Such a being, being unskillful in means (<s>anupāyakuśala</s>) to that extent, will generate false pride (<s>adhimāna</s>). Two stages should be expected for him. Which two? Namely, the <s>Śrāvaka</s> (hearer) stage or the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary buddha) stage. Thus, through the power of truth-adherence (<s>satyādhiṣṭhāna</s>), the activity of <s>Māra</s> (<s>mārakarma</s>) will arise for that <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>. Therein he will not attend upon, not associate with, not serve, not honor spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>). He will tighten that very bondage of <s>Māra</s>. For what reason? Because he has not practiced in the six perfections (<s>ṣaṭpāramitā</s>) and has not been guided by skill in means (<s>upāyakauśala</s>). [f. 215b] Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> thus: If, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, even while within a dream, does not aspire to the level of a <s>Śrāvaka</s> or a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> or the triple world, does not generate a mind seeking personal benefit, views all dharmas as dream-like, views all dharmas as echo-like and up to emanation-like, yet does not realize them directly — this, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be known as the mark of non-regression (<s>avaivartikalakṣaṇa</s>) of a non-regressing <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>. Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, if a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, even while within a dream, sees a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly and fully awakened one, surrounded and attended by a retinue of many hundreds, many thousands, many hundreds of thousands, many <s>koṭis</s>, many thousands of <s>koṭis</s>, many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s>, many <s>niyutas</s> of hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen, <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s>, teaching the Dharma — and having heard that Dharma, thinking 'I shall comprehend the meaning of this Dharma,' dwells practicing in accordance with the Dharma, practicing properly, acting in conformity with the Dharma — this too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be known as the mark of non-regression of a non-regressing <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>. Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, if a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, even while within a dream, sees a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly and fully awakened one, having risen into the sky, teaching the Dharma to the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks, endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great being (

children.translated_text: practice, who practices the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. In what is essential indeed does this <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> practice. When this was said, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said to the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>: In what is inessential indeed, venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, does this <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> practice, who practices the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. For what reason? For, venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is inessential, and all the way to the knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>) is inessential. For what reason? For the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> does not apprehend or perceive what is inessential. How then could he apprehend what is essential? And all the way to: he does not apprehend the inessential knowledge of all aspects. How then could he apprehend what is essential? Then many <s>Devaputras</s> of the desire realm and the form realm thought thus: 'Worthy of homage are those sons and daughters of good family who have generated the thought of unsurpassed perfect awakening and who practice in this profound <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> as taught, and who practice in this meaning, yet do not directly realize the limit of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>) — for by directly realizing it they would remain on the <s>Śrāvaka</s> stage or the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> stage. By this method too, those <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> who do not directly realize this true nature of dharmas are worthy of homage.' This is even more difficult for them, <s>Devaputras</s>: that thinking 'We will lead to <s>Nirvāṇa</s> immeasurable, countless, and limitless beings,' they don the armor (<s>sannāha</s>). Yet those beings are ultimately not apprehended whom they would lead to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. And whatever persons following the <s>Bodhisattva</s> vehicle, <s>Subhūti</s>, turn back — all of them turn back without having attained these mental attentions of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, and they do not know how the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should contemplate dependent origination through the method of accomplishment by the inexhaustibility of space. And whatever persons following the <s>Bodhisattva</s> vehicle, <s>Subhūti</s>, turn back — all of them turn back from unsurpassed perfect awakening without having attained this skill in means (<s>upāyakauśala</s>). And whatever <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, do not turn back from unsurpassed perfect awakening — all of them do not turn back because they have attained this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. And through skill in means, practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> thus, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> should contemplate and accomplish the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> through the method of the inexhaustibility of space. Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> contemplating dependent origination does not see any dharma arising without a cause; does not perceive any dharma as permanent or as ceasing; does not perceive any dharma as a self, as a being, as a living being, as a creature, as a human, as a person, as one who nourishes, as an individual, as a doer, as one who causes to be done, as one who instigates, as one who causes instigation, as an experiencer, as a female experiencer, as a knower, as a seer; does not perceive it as permanent or impermanent, as pleasant or painful, as self or non-self, as peaceful or non-peaceful. Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, should the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> contemplate dependent origination. Here, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, while cultivating wisdom, cultivates that wisdom while dedicating it to omniscience. Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> of the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> reaches fulfillment through cultivation.' The Blessed One said: 'Here, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, while established in the <s>Śīlapāramitā</s>, does not see any dharma as conditioned or unconditioned. Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, while established in the <s>Śīlapāramitā</s>, takes hold of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.' Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, while established in the <s>Kṣāntipāramitā</s>, takes hold of the <s>Śīlapāramitā</s>.' He said: 'How, Blessed One, does the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, while established in the <s>Dhyānapāramitā</s>, take hold of the <s>Kṣāntipāramitā</s>?' The Blessed One said: 'Here, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, while established in the <s>Dhyānapāramitā</s>, examines form as like a mass of foam, feeling as like a bubble, perception as like a mirage, formations as like a plantain tree, and consciousness as like an illusion. For one examining thus, the perception of essencelessness regarding the five aggregates of clinging (<s>upādānaskandha</s>) becomes present. For one examining thus, the thought arises: "When limbs and minor limbs are being cut, who is cut here, and what is being cut? Whose body is it? Whose feeling? Whose perception? Whose formations? Whose consciousness?" For one examining thus, the thought arises: "Who here is being reviled or abused, on account of which ill will would arise in one being reviled or abused?" Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, while established in the <s>Dhyānapāramitā</s>, takes hold of the <s>Kṣāntipāramitā</s>.' He said: 'How, Blessed One, does the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, while established in the <s>Dhyānapāramitā</s>, take hold of the <s>Vīryapāramitā</s>?' body.text: atha khalv āyuṣman subhūtir bhagavantam etad avocat: kiyac ciraṃ saṃprasthito vatāyaṃ bhagavan bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ yo 'nenopāyakauśalena samanvāgataḥ? bhagavān āha: asaṃkhyeyakalpakoṭīniyutasaṃprasthito 'yaṃ subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ yo 'nenopāyakauśalena samanvāgataḥ. āha: kiyanto buddhān bhagavantaḥ paryupāsito 'yaṃ bhagavaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvo yo 'nenopāyakauśalena samanvāgataḥ? bhagavān āha: gaṅgānadīvālukopamān buddhān bhagavantaḥ paryupāsito sa bodhisattvo mahāsattvo veditavyaḥ yo 'nenopāyakauśalena samanvāgataḥ. āha: kin tena bhagavan bodhisattvena mahāsattvena kuśalamūlam avaropitama yo 'nenopāyakauśalena samanvāgataḥ? bhagavān āha: prathamacittotpādam upādāya subhūte na sā kācid dānapāramitā yā tena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena na paripūritā yo 'nenopāyakauśalena samanvāgataḥ. na sā kācic chīlapāramitā kṣāntipāramitā vīryapāramitā dhyānapāramitā prajñāpāramitā yā tena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena na paripūritā yo 'nenopāyakauśalena samanvāgataḥ. āha: āścaryam etad bhagavan bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ ye 'nenopāyakauśalena samanvāgatāḥ. bhagavān āha: evam etat subhūte evam etat. āścaryam etad bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ ye 'nenopāyakauśalena samanvāgatāḥ tadyathāpi nāma subhūte sūryacandramaṇḍalaṃ caturo (

children.text: ) dvīpān avabhāsayati, caluraś ca dvīpān anugacchaty anuparivartate, evam eva subhūte prajñāpāramitā pañcasu pāramitāsu karma karoti, pañcapāramitā anugacchaty anuparivartate. prajñāpāramitā avirahitatvāt pañcapāramitāḥ pāramitānāmadheyaṃ labhante, prajñāpāramitāvirahitatvān na pāramitānāmadheyaṃ labhante. tadyathāpi nāma subhūte yathā rājā cakravartī virahitaḥ saptabhī ratnair na rājā cakravartīti nāmadheyaṃ labhate, evam eva subhūte pañcapāramitā prajñāpāramitāvirahitatvān na pāramitānāmadheyaṃ labhante. tadyathāpi nāma subhūte apuruṣā strī sudharṣaṇā bhavati dhūrtakaiḥ, evam eva subhūte prajñāpāramitāvirahitatvāt pañcapāramitāḥ sudharṣaṇā bhavanti māreṇa vā mārakāyikābhir vā devatābhiḥ. tadyathāpi nāma subhūte saṃgrāmāvacaraḥ puruṣaḥ sarvasannāhasannaddhaḥ saṃgrāme vartamāne durādharṣo bhavati pratirājānair vā pratyarthikair vā pratyamitrair vā, evam eva subhūte pañcapāramitāḥ prajñāpāramitā avirahitatvād durādharṣā bhavanti māreṇa vā mārakāyikābhir vā devatābhir, ādhimānikair vā pudgalair vā, yāvan bodhisattvacaṇḍālair vā. tadyathāpi nāma subhūte koṭṭarājāno rājñā cakravartinā anuvidheyā bhavanti, sāyamprātarupasthānāya gacchanti, evam eva subhūte pañcapāramitāḥ prajñāpāramitāparigṛhītā yena sarvākārajñatā tena anugacchanti. tadyathāpi nāma subhūte yāḥ kācit kunadyaḥ sarvās tā yena gaṅgānadī tena anugacchanti, (
children.translated_text: ) continents, and follows and revolves around the four continents — even so, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> performs its work among the five <s>pāramitās</s>, follows and revolves around the five <s>pāramitās</s>. Through not being separated from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the five <s>pāramitās</s> obtain the designation of "<s>pāramitā</s>"; through being separated from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, they do not obtain the designation of "<s>pāramitā</s>." Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, a universal monarch (<s>cakravartin</s>) separated from the seven treasures does not obtain the designation "universal monarch" — even so, <s>Subhūti</s>, through being separated from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the five <s>pāramitās</s> do not obtain the designation of "<s>pāramitā</s>." Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, a woman without a husband is easily conquered by rascals — even so, <s>Subhūti</s>, through being separated from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the five <s>pāramitās</s> are easily conquered by <s>Māra</s> or by the <s>devatās</s> belonging to <s>Māra</s>'s retinue. Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, a warrior equipped with full armor is, in the midst of battle, unconquerable by rival kings, adversaries, or enemies — even so, <s>Subhūti</s>, through not being separated from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the five <s>pāramitās</s> are unconquerable by <s>Māra</s> or by the <s>devatās</s> belonging to <s>Māra</s>'s retinue, or by conceited persons, or up to by <s>Bodhisattva</s> outcasts. Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, subordinate kings follow the universal monarch, going morning and evening for their audience — even so, <s>Subhūti</s>, the five <s>pāramitās</s>, embraced by the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, follow wherever omniscience (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>) leads. Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, it is the right hand of a person that performs all tasks — even so, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be regarded. As the left hand, so the five <s>pāramitās</s> should be regarded. Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, whatever water is in small rivers and in great rivers — all that water, having entered the great ocean, becomes of one taste — even so, <s>Subhūti</s>, the five <s>pāramitās</s>, embraced by the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, having entered omniscience, obtain the designation of "<s>pāramitā</s>." Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, the wheel-treasure of a universal monarch goes before the fourfold army and stands still, and wherever the universal monarch stops for food, there the wheel-treasure satisfies the army of the universal monarch, and that wheel-treasure does not move from its place — even so, <s>Subhūti</s>, of these five <s>pāramitās</s>, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is the guide: they follow wherever omniscience leads, they abide there, and having abided there, they do not go beyond that place. Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, the wheel-treasure of a universal monarch, and the commander-treasure, and the householder-treasure, and the woman-treasure, and the jewel-treasure, and the elephant-treasure, and the horse-treasure go before the fourfold army — even so, <s>Subhūti</s>, of these five <s>pāramitās</s>, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> goes before them, and having gone before, stands wherever omniscience is. body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> addressed the Blessed One thus: 'How long ago, Blessed One, did this <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> set forth, who is endowed with this skill in means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>)?' The Blessed One said: 'This <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, who is endowed with this skill in means, set forth innumerable <s>koṭī-niyuta kalpas</s> ago.' He said: 'How many Buddhas and Blessed Ones, Blessed One, has this <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> attended upon, who is endowed with this skill in means?' The Blessed One said: 'That <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> who is endowed with this skill in means should be known to have attended upon Buddhas and Blessed Ones as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river.' He said: 'What wholesome root, Blessed One, has been planted by that <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> who is endowed with this skill in means?' body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'Here, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, without apprehending the gift, without apprehending the relinquishment, without apprehending the giver, without apprehending the recipient, gives the gift; without apprehending morality, he guards morality; without apprehending patience, he practices patience; without apprehending vigor, he practices vigor; without apprehending concentration, he practices concentration; without apprehending wisdom, he practices wisdom; without apprehending superknowledges, he practices the superknowledges; without apprehending the foundations of mindfulness, he practices the foundations of mindfulness; and up to: without apprehending the path, he practices the path; and up to: without apprehending emptiness, he practices emptiness; without apprehending the signless, he practices the signless; without apprehending the wishless, he practices the wishless; without apprehending beings, he matures beings; without apprehending a <s>Buddha</s>-field, he purifies a <s>Buddha</s>-field; without apprehending <s>Buddha</s> qualities, he fully awakens to awakening. body.text: bhagavān āha: iha subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattva prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caran yad dānaṃ dadāti tat prajñāpāramitayā parigṛhītaḥ tatra na dvayasaṃjñī bhavati. yac chīlaṃ rakṣati tatra na dvayasaṃjñī bhavati. yat kṣāntiṃ bhāvayati tatra na dvayasaṃjñī bhavati. yad vīryam ārabhate tatra na dvayasaṃjñī bhavati. yad samādhiṃ bhāvayati tatra na dvayasaṃjñī bhavati. yat prajñāṃ bhāvayati tatra na dvayasaṃjñī bhavati. yāvad yad aśītim anuvyañjanāny abhinirhārate. tatra na dvayasaṃjñī bhavati.
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'Here, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, whatever gift he gives — embraced by the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, therein he does not have the perception of duality. Whatever morality he guards, therein he does not have the perception of duality. Whatever patience he cultivates, therein he does not have the perception of duality. Whatever vigor he undertakes, therein he does not have the perception of duality. Whatever concentration he cultivates, therein he does not have the perception of duality. Whatever wisdom he cultivates, therein he does not have the perception of duality. And up to: whatever eighty minor characteristics he produces, therein he does not have the perception of duality.'

body.text: āha: kathaṃ bhagavan bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caran dānaṃ dadāti. tatra ca na dvayasaṃjñī bhavati. yāvad aśītim anuvyañjanāny abhinirhārati. tatra ca na dvayasaṃjñī bhavati?
body.translated_text: He said: 'How, Blessed One, does the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, give the gift and therein not have the perception of duality, and up to produce the eighty minor characteristics and therein not have the perception of duality?'

body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'Here, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, fulfills the perfection of giving. Therein, having included all six <s>pāramitās</s> within the perfection of giving, he gives the gift. Likewise he fulfills all factors conducive to awakening, and up to: therein, having included all six <s>pāramitās</s> within the path, he cultivates the path. And how is that? At the time when the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, gives the gift, he gives the gift while abiding in the undefiled (<s>anāsrava</s>) mind. Abiding in that undefiled mind, he does not perceive any sign: "Who gives? To whom does he give? By what means does he give? What do I give?" With a mind free from signs, with an undefiled mind, free from craving, free from ignorance, he gives the gift. And that

children.translated_text: cultivates patience, undertakes vigor, cultivates concentration, and cultivates wisdom. Likewise, standing in the five aggregates that are like a reflection, like a mirage, like a magical illusion, like a magical creation, he gives the gift, guards morality, cultivates patience, undertakes vigor, cultivates concentration, and cultivates wisdom. The five aggregates that are dream-like are without characteristics; the five aggregates that are echo-like, reflection-like, mirage-like, illusion-like, and creation-like are without characteristics. For what reason? For a dream has no inherent nature, a reflection has no inherent nature, a mirage has no inherent nature, a magical illusion has no inherent nature, a magical creation has no inherent nature. That which has no inherent nature has no characteristic; that which has no characteristic has a single characteristic — namely, no characteristic. By this method too, <s>Subhūti</s>, it should be understood thus: the gift is without characteristics, the giver is without characteristics, the recipient is without characteristics. He who, knowing thus, gives the gift, fulfills the perfection of giving and does not turn away from the perfection of morality, nor from the perfection of patience, vigor, concentration, or wisdom. Standing here in the six <s>pāramitās</s>, he fulfills the four <s>dhyānas</s>, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of supernatural power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the noble eightfold path. He fulfills the emptiness of the internal, the emptiness of the external, the emptiness of the internal and external, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of inherent nature, the emptiness of the non-existence of inherent nature, and up to the emptiness of own-characteristics. He fulfills the concentration on emptiness, the signless concentration, and the wishless concentration. He fulfills the eight liberations, the nine successive attainments, the five superknowledges, and the five hundred gates of <s>dhāraṇī</s>. He fulfills the four analytical knowledges (

Abiding in the diamond-like <s>samādhi</s>, setting aside the <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>samādhi</s>, whatever <s>samādhis</s> there are — whether shared with <s>śrāvakas</s> or shared with <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, or whatever other groups of <s>samādhi</s>-attainments — he pervades them all with his body, enters and abides in them. Yet he does not savor those <s>samādhis</s>, nor the fruit of attainment. For what reason? For that <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> knows those <s>samādhis</s> to be without characteristics and without inherent nature. How then can a <s>dharma</s> without characteristics savor a <s>dharma</s> without characteristics? How can a <s>dharma</s> without inherent existence savor a <s>dharma</s> without inherent existence? Thus, not savoring, he is not reborn through the power of any <s>samādhi</s> — neither in the form realm nor in the formless realm. For what reason? For he does not apprehend those two realms. Nor does he apprehend one who would attain or that by which one would attain. Thus, not apprehending, he fulfills the <s>samādhipāramitā</s> (perfection of concentration) that is without characteristics. Through this <s>samādhipāramitā</s>, he transcends the levels of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>

body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, how does a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, abiding in the five <s>upādānaskandhas</s> (aggregates of clinging) that are like a dream, abiding in the five <s>upādānaskandhas</s> that are like an echo, like a reflection, like an illusion, like a mirage, and like an emanation, fulfill the <s>samādhipāramitā</s> (perfection of concentration)? And how, <s>Subhūti</s>, does a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, abiding in the five <s>upādānaskandhas</s> that are like a dream, like an echo, like a reflection, like an illusion, like a mirage, and like an emanation, fulfill the <s>samādhipāramitā</s>? Here, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> enters and abides in the first <s>dhyāna</s>, up to the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>. He enters and abides in <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), <s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy), and <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity). He enters and abides in the sphere of infinite space, the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, and the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. body.text: subhūtir āha: kathaṃ bhagavaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattva samādhipāramitāṃ paripūrya śrāvakapratyekabuddhabhūmī atikrāmati?
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: How, <s>Bhagavan</s>, does a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, having fulfilled the <s>samādhipāramitā</s>, transcend the levels of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>?

body.text: bhagavān āha: tathā hi subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'dhyātmaśūnyatāyāṃ suśikṣitaḥ yāvat svalakṣaṇaśūnyatāyāṃ suśikṣitaḥ, na ceha śūnyatāsu kaścid dharma upalabbyate. yatra pratiṣṭhet. srotaāpattiphalaṃ vā sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ vā anāgāmiphalaṃ vā arhattvaṃ vā pratyekabodhiṃ vā, yāpi sā sarvākārajñatā sāpi śūnyā śūnyatābhiḥ. sa ābhiḥ śūnyatābhiḥ bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhabhūmī atikramya bodhisattvanyāmam avakrāmati.
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is well-trained in <s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s> (internal emptiness), up to <s>svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of own-characteristics). And in these emptinesses, no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever is apprehended wherein one might establish oneself — neither the fruit of stream-entry, nor the fruit of once-returning, nor the fruit of non-returning, nor <s>arhatship</s>, nor <s>pratyekabodhi</s> (solitary awakening). Even that <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects) is itself empty through these emptinesses. Through these emptinesses, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, transcending the levels of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, enters the <s>bodhisattva-nyāma</s> (the fixed course of the bodhisattva).

body.text: āha: katamo bhagavan bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya āma katamo nyāmaḥ?
body.translated_text: He said: What, <s>Bhagavan</s>, is the <s>āma</s> (unfixed course) of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, and what is the <s>nyāma</s> (fixed course)?

body.text: bhagavān āha: sarvaḥ subhūte bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya upalaṃbhaḥ. āmaḥ, sarvonupalaṃbho nyāmaḥ.
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: All apprehension, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the <s>āma</s> (unfixed course) of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. All non-apprehension is the <s>nyāma</s> (fixed course).

body.text: āha: katamo bhagavann upalaṃbhaḥ katamo 'nupalaṃbhaḥ?
body.translated_text: He said: What, <s>Bhagavan</s>, is apprehension, and what is non-apprehension?

body.text: (VIII 4) atha āyuṣmān subhūtir bhagavantam etad avocat: kathaṃ bhagavan svapnopamānāṃ sarvadharmāṇām avastukānām abhāvasvabhāvānāṃ svalakṣaṇaśūnyānāṃ vyavasthānaṃ bhavati. ime kuśalā dharmā ime akuśalā dharmā ime laukikā ime lokottarā ime sāsravā ime anāsravā ime saṃskṛtā ime asaṃskṛtā ime srotaāpattiphalasākṣātkriyāyai saṃvartante. ime sakṛdāgāmiphalasākṣātkriyāyai ime 'nāgāmiphalasākṣātkriyāyai ime 'rhatphalasākṣātkriyāyai saṃvartante. ime pratyekabodhaye saṃvartante. ime 'nuttarasyai samyaksaṃbodhaye saṃvartante? evaṃ kathaṃ pratiśrutkopmānāṃ pratibhāsopamānāṃmāyopamānāṃ marīcyupamānāṃ nirmitopamānām avastukānām abhāvasvabhāvānāṃ svalaksaṇaśūnyānāṃ vyavasthānaṃ bhavati. ime kuśalā dharmā ime akuśalā yāvad ime 'nuttarasyai samyaksaṃbodhaye saṃvartante?
body.translated_text: (VIII 4) Then the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> addressed the Blessed One thus: 'How, Blessed One, is there a determination of all dharmas that are dream-like, without substance, devoid of inherent nature, and empty of their own characteristics — that "these are wholesome dharmas, these are unwholesome dharmas, these are mundane, these are supramundane, these are defiled, these are undefiled, these are conditioned, these are unconditioned, these conduce to the realization of the fruit of stream-entry, these to the fruit of once-returning, these to the fruit of non-returning, these conduce to the realization of the fruit of <s>Arhat</s>ship, these conduce to <s>Pratyekabodhi</s>, these conduce to unsurpassed perfect and full awakening"? Likewise, how is there a determination of all dharmas that are echo-like, reflection-like, illusion-like, mirage-like, and magical-creation-like, that are without substance, devoid of inherent nature, and empty of their own characteristics — that "these are wholesome dharmas, these are unwholesome, up to these conduce to unsurpassed perfect and full awakening"?'

body.translated_text: (VIII 5, le) 'Here, <s>Subhūti</s>, looking out upon the world with the <s>Buddha</s>-eye, I saw <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> in the eastern direction, in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river, gathering human beings through the four means of gathering (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>). Which four? (I) giving (<s>dāna</s>), (II) kind speech (<s>priyavadyatā</s>), (III) beneficial conduct (<s>arthacaryā</s>), (IV) consistency of aim (<s>samanārthatā</s>). [see on pp. 43-4. E.C.]

body.text: (I) kathaṃ ca subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattva dānena sattvān saṃgṛhṇāti? iha subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvo dvābhyāṃ dānābhyāṃ sattvān saṃgṛhṇāti. katamābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ? yaduta (la) āmiṣadānena ca (Ib) dharmadānena ca.
body.translated_text: (I) And how, <s>Subhūti</s>, does the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> gather beings through giving? Here, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> gathers beings through two kinds of giving. Which two? Namely, (Ia) the giving of material things (<s>āmiṣadāna</s>) and (Ib) the giving of the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmadāna</s>).

body.translated_text: (A) 'And which are the three concentrations? The concentration on emptiness (<s>śūnyatāsamādhi</s>), the signless concentration (<s>ānimittasamādhi</s>), and the wishless concentration (<s>apraṇihitasamādhi</s>). And what is the concentration on emptiness? That one-pointedness of mind through the aspect of emptiness and the aspect of isolation — this is called the concentration on emptiness. And what is the signless concentration? That one-pointedness of mind through the aspect of peace — this is called the signless concentration. And what is the wishless concentration? That one-pointedness of mind through the aspect of impermanence and the aspect of suffering — this is called the wishless concentration.'

Up to all dharmas are not one thing and the <s>dharmadhātu</s> another, <s>tathatā</s> another, <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> another.'

body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'But, <s>Subhūti</s>, do foolish ordinary persons comprehend conventional truth or ultimate truth? If they do comprehend, then there will be a determination of fruits for them too — the fruit of stream-entry, or the fruit of once-returning, or the fruit of non-returning, or <s>Arhat</s>ship, or <s>Pratyekabodhi</s>, or perfect awakening. But, <s>Subhūti</s>, since foolish ordinary persons have no path, no determination of the path, and no cultivation of the path, how then will there be a determination of fruits for foolish ordinary persons? For noble persons, however, there is a path and cultivation of the path. Therefore, for noble persons there will be a determination of fruits.'

body.text: āha: kiṃ punar bhagavan mārgabhāvanāyā phalaprāptir bhavati. phalaṃ vā prāpyate?
body.translated_text: He said: 'But, Blessed One, is it through the cultivation of the path that there is attainment of the fruit? Or is the fruit attained?'

body.text: bhagavān āha: no hīdaṃ subhūte, na mārgabhāvanāyā phalaprāptir bhavati. phalaṃ vā prāpyate. na punaḥ subhūte abhāvitamārgasya phalaprāptir na mārgeṇa phalaṃ prāpsyate. evaṃ hi subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caran sattvānāṃ phalavyavasthānaṃ karoti. na ca bhāgacchedena saṃskṛtadhātor vā asaṃskṛtadhātor vā phalavyavasthānam.
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'No indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>. It is not through the cultivation of the path that there is attainment of the fruit, nor is the fruit attained. But, <s>Subhūti</s>, without having cultivated the path, there is no attainment of the fruit, nor is the fruit attained through the path. Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, while practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, makes a determination of fruits for beings — not, however, by a cutting off of portions from the conditioned realm or the unconditioned realm is there a determination of fruits.'

body.text: bhagavān āha: evaṃ khalu subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caran sattvānāṃ dharman deśayaty abhāgacchedatām upādāya. yaduta adhyātmaśūnyatām upādāya. yāvat svalakṣaṇaśūnyatām upādāya. ātmanā ca na kvacid dharme 'bhiniviśate. paraṃ ca na kvacid abhiniveśayati. dānapāramitāyāṃ vā śīlapāramitāyāṃ vā kṣāntipāramitāyāṃ vā vīryapāramitāyāṃ vā dhyānapāramitāyāṃ vā prajñāpāramitāyāṃ vā, prathame vā dhyāne yāvac caturthe vā dhyāne. maitryāṃ vā karuṇāyāṃ vā muditāyāṃ vā upekṣāyāṃ vā yāvan naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanasamāpattau vā smṛtyupasthāneṣu vā. yāvad āryāṣṭāṅge mārge. yāvat sarvākārajñatāyāṃ vā, so 'nabhiniviṣṭo na kvacit sajjate. tadyathāpi nāma tathāgatanirmito dānaṃ ca dadāti na ca dānaphale sajjate. na dānaphalaṃ pratyanubhavaty anyatra sarvasattvānāṃ parinirvāpanārthaṃ. yāvat ṣaṭsu pāramitāsu yāvat sāsravānāsraveṣu dharmeṣu laukikalokottareṣu saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛteṣu na kvacit tiṣṭhati. evam eva subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caran sarvadharmeṣu carati. na kvacid dharme tiṣṭhati na sajjate. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hy asya dharmāṇāṃ dharmalakṣaṇaṃ supratividdhaṃ.
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, while practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, teaches the Dharma to beings on the basis of non-cutting-off of portions — namely, on the basis of the emptiness of the internal, up to the emptiness of individual characteristics. One does not oneself cling to any dharma, nor does one cause others to cling — whether in the <s>Dānapāramitā</s>, <s>Śīlapāramitā</s>, <s>Kṣāntipāramitā</s>, <s>Vīryapāramitā</s>, <s>Dhyānapāramitā</s>, or <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>; in the first <s>dhyāna</s> up to the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>; in loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, or equanimity; up to the attainment of neither-perception-nor-non-perception; in the foundations of mindfulness; up to the noble eightfold path; up to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects) — one who does not cling is not attached anywhere. Just as a <s>Tathāgata</s>-emanation gives gifts yet is not attached to the fruit of giving, and does not experience the fruit of giving except for the purpose of leading all beings to <s>parinirvāṇa</s>; up to in the six <s>pāramitās</s>, up to in dharmas with and without outflows, mundane and supramundane, conditioned and unconditioned, it abides nowhere. Just so, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, while practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, moves among all dharmas yet abides in no dharma and is not attached. For what reason? For the dharma-characteristic of dharmas has been well penetrated by this one.'

body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'Just so, <s>Subhūti</s>, just so. No being has been apprehended by the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> whom one would liberate from the triple world. And purify Buddha-fields and ripen beings?'

children.translated_text: naming arises from conceptualization. Do not be attached to conceptualization. In the absence of substance, which is empty of inherent nature — for the wise do not cling to empty dharmas." Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, while practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, teaches the Dharma to beings with skillful means. What, <s>Subhūti</s>, is a sign? There are two kinds of signs, <s>Subhūti</s>, to which foolish ordinary persons are attached. What are the two? Namely, the sign of form and the sign of the formless. And what, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the sign of form? Whatever form, <s>Subhūti</s>, is gross or subtle, inferior or superior — when in these momentary dharmas there is grasping through conceptualization, this is called the sign of form. And what, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the sign of the formless? When through grasping at the sign of formless dharmas, defilement arises through conceptualization, this is called the sign of the formless. The <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, while practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, with skillful means, separating beings from that sign, establishes and stations them in the signless realm — and so establishes and stations them that they do not fall into the duality: "This is a sign, this is the signless." Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, while practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (
AdSPG II 63
), with skillful means, separates beings
from signs and establishes them in the signless realm.'

children.translated_text: ) water in a mirage is utterly not found, so he comprehends perception. It does not come from anywhere nor go anywhere. Thus he comprehends the arising and passing away of perception. And how does he comprehend the <s>tathatā</s> of perception? Just as the <s>tathatā</s> of feeling, so he comprehends the <s>tathatā</s> of perception. How does he comprehend formations? Just as the essence of a plantain tree, when examined leaf by leaf, is not found to be substantial, so he comprehends formations. How does he comprehend the arising and passing away of formations? Through their not coming from anywhere and not going anywhere, he comprehends the arising and passing away of formations. And how does he comprehend the <s>tathatā</s> of formations? Through the <s>tathatā</s> of feeling, he comprehends the <s>tathatā</s> of formations. How does he comprehend consciousness? Just as a magician's creation of a fourfold army, so he comprehends consciousness. It does not come from anywhere nor go anywhere. Thus he comprehends the arising and passing away of consciousness. How does he comprehend the <s>tathatā</s> of consciousness? Through the <s>tathatā</s> of feeling, he comprehends the <s>tathatā</s> of consciousness. And how does he comprehend the elements? The eye-element is empty of the inherent nature of the eye-element. The form-element is empty of the inherent nature of the form-element. The eye-consciousness-element is empty of the inherent nature of the eye-consciousness-element. Thus, up to the mind-element, the dharma-element, and the mind-consciousness-element should be understood. And how does he comprehend the sense bases? Internal dharmas are empty of internal dharmas; external dharmas are empty of external dharmas. Thus he comprehends the sense bases. And how does he comprehend the noble truth? He comprehends suffering, comprehends the truth, comprehends the noble truth. He comprehends the noble truth as freed from duality, for the truth of the noble ones is non-dual. Thus he comprehends the origin, cessation, and the path leading to cessation as noble truths. How does he comprehend the <s>tathatā</s> of suffering?

children.translated_text: He comprehends <s>tathatā</s> itself as the <s>tathatā</s> of suffering. Thus he comprehends the <s>tathatā</s> of origin, cessation, and the path. And how does he comprehend <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination)? He comprehends dependent origination as non-arising. Thus, as non-ceasing, non-annihilated, non-eternal, not of one meaning, not of many meanings, without coming, without going, the cessation of conceptual proliferation — he comprehends dependent origination as peaceful. Thus he comprehends dependent origination.'

body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'Here, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, while practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, comprehends form — how form arises, how form ceases, and what is the <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of form. How does he comprehend form? As utterly porous and utterly hollow. Just as a lump of foam is without essence, so he comprehends form. And how does he comprehend [f. 285b] the arising of form? Those Buddhas and Blessed Ones who existed in the past — their <s>Buddhanetrī</s> too was <s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s>. Those Buddhas and Blessed Ones who will exist in the future — their <s>Buddhanetrī</s> too will be <s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s>. body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'It is so, <s>Subhūti</s>, it is so. When all dharmas are insubstantial, what being is there whom the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> would establish in the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, <s>Arhat</s>ship, <s>Pratyekabodhi</s>, or unsurpassed perfect and full awakening? It is only that one who is enveloped by perversion is established and stationed in the non-perverse through wisdom. That very perversion is non-perversion, taking it as the outflow of conceptualization. And the non-conceptual is the non-perverse — where there is no perversion, there is no self, no being, up to no progenitor, no observer; there is no form, no feeling, no perception, no formations, no consciousness, up to no awakening. children.translated_text: how much less the ordinary person's dharmas. For what reason? For, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, no dharma whatsoever has an inherent nature. When all dharmas are thus without inherent nature, which is the ordinary person? Which is the stream-enterer? Which is the once-returner? Which is the non-returner? Which is the <s>Arhat</s>? Which is the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>? Which is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>? Which is the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One? If these persons are not apprehended, how will there be a manifestation of those dharmas by which one is designated as an ordinary person, or a stream-enterer, up to an <s>Arhat</s>, or a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, or a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, or a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Enlightened One?'

body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'So it is, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, so it is, just as you say. Without training in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> cannot awaken to unsurpassed perfect and full awakening. But that is through skillful means, not through unskillful means. If, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, while practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, were to apprehend the inherent nature of any dharma, he would grasp it. But he does not apprehend it. Then what will he grasp? "This is the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, this is the <s>Samādhipāramitā</s>, this is the <s>Vīryapāramitā</s>, this is the <s>Kṣāntipāramitā</s>, this is the <s>Śīlapāramitā</s>, this is the <s>Dānapāramitā</s>, this is form, up to this is consciousness, up to these are the Buddha-dharmas" — up to he does not even apprehend a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Then what will he grasp? Ungraspable, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, is the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Up to ungraspable are the Buddha-dharmas. This, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, is the ungraspable <s>Pāramitā</s> — namely, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Herein the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> should train. While training herein, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> will not apprehend even the training — how much less awakening, how much less the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, how much less the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-dharmas,

body.translated_text: (VIII 5,11) He said: 'What, Blessed One, is the skillful means of the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> by which the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, seeing all dharmas as without substance, becomes established in unsurpassed perfect and full awakening?'

body.text: bhagavān āha: iha śāradvatīputra bodhisattvo mahāsattva prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caran na kasyacid dharmasya vastu samanupaśyati. yatra vastuni pratihanyeta, yatra vā pratihanyamāno 'valīyeta: avalīyamānaḥ saṃsīdet saṃsīdan visīded visīdaṃ kausīdyam āpadyeta: yasmāt tarhi śāradvatīputra avastukā ajīvā nirjīvā. abhāvasvabhāvā prakṛtiśūnyāḥ svalakṣaṇaśūnyā. sarvadharmāḥ, anyatra saṃmohe na sattvā abhiniviṣṭā skandhā iti vā dhātava iti vā āyatanāni iti vā, tad bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ abhāvasvabhāvān sarvadharmān saṃpaśyan prakṛtiśūnyān svalakṣaṇaśūnyān prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caran. māyākārasadṛśam ātmabhāvam adhiṣṭhāya sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati. ye sattvā matsariṇo bhavanti. teṣān dānakathāṃ karoti, duśśīlānāṃ śīlakathāṃ vyāpannacittānāṃ kṣāntikathāṃ kusīdānāṃ vīryakathāṃ vikṣiptacittānāṃ samādhikathāṃ duṣprajñānāṃ prajñākathāṃ karoti. yadā te sattvā dāne pratiṣṭhāpitā bhavanti. yāvad prajñāpāramitāyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpitā bhavanti. tadā teṣāṃ (

body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'Here, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, while practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, does not perceive any substance in any dharma — whereby he might be obstructed, or whereby, being obstructed, he might retreat; retreating, he might sink down; sinking down, he might become despondent; becoming despondent, he might fall into indolence. Since, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, all dharmas are without substance, without life, without soul, of non-existent inherent nature, empty by nature, and empty of own-characteristic — except through delusion, beings are not attached to "aggregates" or "elements" or "sense-bases" — therefore the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, seeing all dharmas as of non-existent inherent nature, empty by nature, empty of own-characteristic, while practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, having assumed a person like a magician's creation, teaches the Dharma to beings. To those beings who are miserly, he gives a discourse on giving; to those of bad morality, a discourse on morality; to those of hostile mind, a discourse on patience; to the indolent, a discourse on vigor; to those of distracted mind, a discourse on <s>samādhi</s>; to those of poor wisdom, a discourse on wisdom. children.translated_text: "O beings, why do you not cultivate the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>?" They say thus: "Because of a deficiency of conditions." Thereupon the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, abiding in the <s>Dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of giving), admonishes beings thus: "Receive provisions from me. Having received provisions from me, give gifts, guard moral conduct, cultivate patience, undertake vigor, enter into concentration." Then, having fulfilled these aspects, reflect thus: "Is any dharma apprehended when the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is being taught — a self, a being, up to an agent, an instigator, form, feeling, perception, formations, consciousness, the desire realm, the form realm, the formless realm, all the <s>Pāramitās</s>, the thirty-seven factors conducive to awakening, the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, <s>Arhat</s>ship, <s>Pratyekabodhi</s>, up to unsurpassed perfect and full awakening?" Thereupon the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, while practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, does not apprehend any dharma by apprehending which he would cling. He, not clinging, does not perceive the arising or cessation or defilement or purification of any dharma. He, not apprehending, does not discriminate: "This one is a hell-being, or an animal, or in the world of <s>Yama</s>, or an <s>asura</s>, or a god, or a human; this one is moral or immoral; this one is a stream-enterer, this one a once-returner, this one a non-returner, this one an <s>Arhat</s>, this one a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, this one a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One." Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, abiding in the <s>Dānapāramitā</s>, gathers beings into the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. And how, <s>Subhūti</s>, does the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, abiding in the <s>Dānapāramitā</s>, the <s>Śīlapāramitā</s>, the <s>Kṣāntipāramitā</s>, the <s>Vīryapāramitā</s>, the <s>Dhyānapāramitā</s>, and the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, embrace up to the thirty-seven factors conducive to awakening? Emptiness does not cling to emptiness; emptiness itself is not even apprehended — how much less one who would cling to emptiness! Thus the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, without clinging, abides in all dharmas. Abiding in that training, he surveys all conduct: 'Where do these beings dwell in wrong grasping?' Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> thinks: 'These beings are indeed easy to liberate from wrong grasping.' Then, through skillful means, abiding in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, he admonishes thus: 'Come, O beings, give gifts! That will be your abundance of possessions. But do not be proud of those possessions — there is no essence therein.' Likewise he admonishes regarding moral conduct: 'Come, O beings, guard moral conduct! But do not be proud of that moral conduct — there is no essence therein.' Likewise he admonishes regarding patience, vigor, and concentration: 'Come, O beings, enter into concentration! body.text: bhagavān āha: na subhūte mārgeṇa bodhiḥ prāpyate. na amārgeṇa. bodhir eva mārgo mārga eva bodhiḥ.
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: '<s>Subhūti</s>, awakening is not attained through the path, nor through the non-path. Awakening itself is the path; the path itself is awakening.'

body.text: āha: yadi bhagavaṃ bodhir eva mārgo mārga eva bodhiḥ, tat prāptaiva bhavati bodhisattvena mahāsattvena bodhiḥ, tat kathaṃ tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho nirdiśyate. dvātṛṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇair daśabhis tathāgatabalaiś caturbhir vaiśāradyaiś catasṛbhiḥ pratisaṃvidbhir yāvad aṣṭādaśabhir āveṇikair buddhadharmaiḥ?
body.translated_text: He said: 'If, Blessed One, awakening itself is the path and the path itself is awakening, then awakening has already been attained by the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>. Then how is the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Enlightened One described with the thirty-two marks of a great person, the ten <s>Tathāgata</s> powers, the four confidences, the four analytical knowledges, up to the eighteen special Buddha-dharmas?'

body.text: bhagavān āha: [f. 297a] tat kiṃ manyase subhūte buddho bodhiṃ prāpnoti?
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: [f. 297a] 'What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>? Does a Buddha attain awakening?'

body.text: āha: no hīdaṃ bhagavaṃ, na buddho bodhiṃ prāpnoti. buddha eva bodhir bodhir eva buddhaḥ.
body.translated_text: He said: 'No indeed, Blessed One. A Buddha does not attain awakening. The Buddha itself is awakening; awakening itself is the Buddha.'

One is oneself endowed with all roots of merit and makes all those beings endowed with roots of merit. One's body is beautiful — both one's own and that of those beings who have been ripened by that <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>. For them, a beautiful, attractive, inspiring body is produced — because it is embraced by merit. Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> purifies the Buddha-field. And so purifies it that even the designation of the three lower realms of existence will not exist; the designation of wrong views will not exist; the designation of desire, aversion, and delusion will not exist; the designation of woman and man will not exist; the designation of the two vehicles will not exist; the designation of impermanence, suffering, and non-self will not exist; the designation of possession will not exist; the designation of the notion of "I" and "mine" will not exist; the designation of latent tendencies and their arising will not exist; the designation of perversions will not exist; the designation of determination of fruits will not exist. Only the sound of the <s>samādhi</s> of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness

body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'Is there, <s>Subhūti</s>, any dharma that is not included in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>?'

body.text: āha: yadi bhagavaṃ. prajñāpāramitā svabhāvena śūnyā kathaṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ sarvadharmā antargatā? na ca bhagavaṃc chūnyatāyāṃ kaścid dharmo 'ntargato vā na vā antargataḥ.
body.translated_text: He said: 'If, Blessed One, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is empty by inherent nature, how are all dharmas included in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>? For, Blessed One, in emptiness no dharma is either included or not included.'

body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'Are not, <s>Subhūti</s>, all dharmas empty of all dharmas?'

body.text: āha: śūnyā bhagavaṃ.
body.translated_text: He said: 'They are empty, Blessed One.'

body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'If, <s>Subhūti</s>, all dharmas are empty of all dharmas, then are not all dharmas included in emptiness?'

body.text: āha: evam etad bhagavan.
body.translated_text: He said: 'It is so, Blessed One.'

body.text: bhagavān āha: tad anena subhūte paryāyeṇa evaṃ veditavyaṃ, yat prajñāpāramitāyāṃ sthitvā bodhisattvo mahāsattva idam evaṃrūpam upāyakauśalaṃ kurute.
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'By this method, <s>Subhūti</s>, it should be understood that, established in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> performs these kinds of skillful means.'

body.text: (VIII 5,18) athāyuṣmān subhūtir bhagavantam etad avocat: kathaṃ bhagavaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattva prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caran sarvadharmaśūnyatāyāṃ sthitvā abhijñāpāramitām abhinirmāti? yāsv abhijñāsu sthitvā pūrvasyān diśi gaṅgānadīvālukopamān lokadhātūn gacchati. tatra lokadhātuṣu ye buddhā bhagavantas tiṣṭhanti dhṛyante yāpayanti dharmañ ca deśayanti tāṃ. paryupāste dharmaṃ ca śṛṇoti. tatra ca buddheṣu bhagavatsu kuśalamūlāny avaropayati?
body.translated_text: (VIII 5,18) Then the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> addressed the Blessed One thus: 'How, Blessed One, does the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, while practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, established in the emptiness of all dharmas, accomplish the perfection of superknowledges (<s>abhijñāpāramitā</s>)? Established in which superknowledges, he goes to world-realms as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the eastern direction, and in those world-realms, attends upon the Buddhas and Blessed Ones who abide, endure, and live there and teach the Dharma, hears the Dharma, and plants roots of wholesome merit in those Buddhas and Blessed Ones?'

children.translated_text: To those beings of bad morality, he teaches the Dharma thus: 'Suffering indeed, good people, is immorality. For the immoral one cannot accomplish even his own welfare, let alone another's. The ripening of immorality is hell, animal birth, or the world of <s>Yama</s>. If you have fallen into the three lower realms, you cannot even accomplish your own welfare, let alone another's. Therefore, you should not give even a single moment's opportunity to an immoral thought, lest you later feel remorse.' To those beings who are hostile toward one another, he teaches the Dharma thus: 'Do not be hostile to each other! For those who have agitated minds, no wholesome dharma arises. body.translated_text: (VIII 5,24) Then the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> addressed the Blessed One thus: 'One who sees reality (<s>bhūtadarśin</s>), Blessed One, is neither defiled nor purified. Even one who does not see reality is neither defiled nor purified. For all dharmas are without inherent nature of existence. And, Blessed One, for non-existence there is no defilement and no purification. For existence too, Blessed One, there is no defilement and no purification. For inherent nature too, Blessed One, there is no defilement and no purification. For the non-existence of inherent nature too, Blessed One, there is no defilement and no purification. Then, as for this purification that the Blessed One has taught, what does it mean, Blessed One?'

body.text: bhagavān āha: yā eṣāṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ samatā tan mayoktaṃ vyavadānaṃ?
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'The equality (<s>samatā</s>) of all these dharmas — that is what I have called purification.'

body.text: āha: sā punaḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ samatā katamā?

body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: '<s>Tathatā</s> (suchness), <s>avitathatā</s> (non-otherness of suchness), <s>ananyatathatā</s> (non-difference of suchness), <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature of dharmas), <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of dharmas), <s>dharmasthititā</s> (stability of dharmas), <s>dharmaniyāmatā</s> (fixed order of dharmas), <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> (limit of reality) — that which, whether <s>Tathāgatas</s> arise or <s>Tathāgatas</s> do not arise, remains as the established realm of the stability of dharmas, namely the <s>dharmadhātu</s> — this, <s>Subhūti</s>, is purification. But it is expressed through worldly convention. It is inexpressible, unutterable, beyond all paths of words, sounds, and speech.'
